Torneko fought monsters and brought
fresh happiness to the people.

entries.english: Tessie: "I tried sleeping, but nothing changed. So this really isn't a dream."

entries.before: Tessie: "Oh! You are awake too!"
entries.english: Tessie: "Oh! You're awake too!"

entries.english: Tessie: "But I believe in you. Whatever happens, I know you'll save us."

ネネ「もしかしたら　ポポロが見た
<TAB>ふしぎな夢って　あの嵐のこと
<TAB>だったのかもしれないでしょ。
entries.before: Tessie: "Perhaps that strange dream Tipper had was about the storm."
entries.english: Tessie: "Maybe that strange dream Tipper had was about the storm."
entries.reason: Natural tentative speculation.

entries.japanese:
ネネ「まあ　そんなことが……。
<TAB>でも　ポポロのことも
<TAB>考えてくださるのね？
entries.before: Tessie: "Goodness... But he will think about how to help Tipper too?"
entries.english: Tessie: "Goodness... But he'll still try to think of a way to help Tipper, won't he?"
entries.reason: Express her request for reassurance naturally; 考えてくださる is considering a way to help.

entries.japanese:
ネネ「あら　あなた　目が覚めたのね。
<TAB>ちょうど　いま　族長さまと　お孫さんが
<TAB>いらっしゃったところよ。
entries.before: Tessie: "Oh, you are awake! The chief and his grandchildren have just arrived."
entries.english: Tessie: "Oh, you're awake! The chief and his grandchildren have just arrived."
entries.reason: Natural family dialogue.

entries.japanese:
族長「トルネコどのの　お供で
<TAB>修行させていただくのは　たいへん
<TAB>ありがたいことでは　ありますが……。
entries.before: Chief: "I would be grateful for him to learn by travelling with you, of course..."
entries.english: Chief: "I am grateful for the chance for him to learn by travelling with you, of course..."
entries.reason: Remove the unnatural construction grateful for him to learn; retain gratitude and reservation.

entries.japanese:
ネネ「あなたのことだから　心配は
<TAB>してないけど……。
<TAB>どうか　無理はしないでね。
entries.before: Tessie: "I know you can take care of yourself... Just do not push yourself too hard."
entries.english: Tessie: "I know you can take care of yourself... Just don't push yourself too hard."
entries.reason: Natural family dialogue.

entries.japanese:
ネネ「どうか　無理はしないでね。
<TAB>教会や　神父さまを見かけたら
<TAB>忘れずに　お祈りするのよ。
entries.before: Tessie: "Please do not overdo it. If you see a church or a priest, remember to pray."
entries.english: Tessie: "Please don't overdo it. If you see a church or a priest, remember to pray."
entries.reason: Natural family dialogue, preserving save-related advice.

entries.japanese:
ネネ「いよいよ　行くのね。
<TAB>あなたのことだから

entries.before: Tessie: "So you are leaving at last. I know you can take care of yourself, but..."
entries.english: Tessie: "So you're leaving at last. I know you can take care of yourself, but..."
entries.reason: Natural family dialogue.

entries.japanese:

<TAB>心配だわ。　トルネコさん　いそいで

entries.before: Ines: "He really will not wake up... How worrying. Let us hurry to the northern shrine."
entries.english: Ines: "He really won't wake up... I'm worried. Let's hurry to the northern shrine."
entries.reason: Avoid detached How worrying when Ines is expressing personal concern.

ネネ「じゃあ　ポポロと　いっしょに
<TAB>寝ましょうね。

entries.english: Tessie: "Let's get some sleep with Tipper, then. Good night, dear..."
entries.reason: Natural family dialogue.

entries.english: Chief: "They say maze entrances appear outside the village and drag travellers into the dark."

entries.english: ???: "S-something terrible has happened! I went to check the northern shrine this morning..."

entries.japanese:
族長「それが　真実のトビラの向こう
<TAB>でのことだったのなら　ともかく
<TAB>どうか　お気になさらず。
entries.before: Chief: "If it happened beyond the Gate of Truth... Well, please do not trouble yourself."
entries.english: Chief: "If it happened beyond the Gate of Truth... Well, please do not let it worry you."

entries.english: Ines: "For now, let's hurry underground. The stairs should be on the left of the passage."

<TAB>（中略）

<TAB>私も　畑仕事を　がんばろうと
<TAB>思ったんですけどね……。

entries.english: ???: "I wanted to follow my brother's example by working hard in the fields, but..."
entries.reason: The brother is a lighthouse keeper, not another farm worker; keep the comparison about diligence.

りっぱな　若き王と　その臣下が
描かれている。
entries.before: It depicts a distinguished young king and his subjects.
entries.english: It depicts a distinguished young king and his retainers.
entries.reason: 臣下 are the king's retainers, more specific than all his subjects.

entries.english: Captain: "In fact, we have already sought applicants and arranged the interviews."
entries.reason: Use the natural collocation arranged interviews.

イネス「なんだか　おかしなことに
<TAB>なっちゃったわね。

entries.english: Ines: "Well, that took a strange turn. Good work, Torneko."
entries.reason: おつかれさま acknowledges his effort; avoid an unnecessary assertion about fatigue.

兵士長「な　なんという男だ……。
<TAB>あんなヤツを　やとうとは

entries.english: Captain: "U-unbelievable... Are you truly going to hire that fellow, Torneko?"

兵士長「な　なんという男だ……。
<TAB>これは　もう　店員は
<TAB>サムソンに　決まりですな？
entries.before: Captain: "Wh-what a man... Well, that settles it. You'll hire Samson, won't you?"
entries.english: Captain: "U-unbelievable... Well, that settles it. You'll hire Samson, won't you?"
entries.reason: Match the captain's disapproval of Douglas in the alternate branch.

entries.japanese:
ダグラス「あんた　店が　もうかるなら
<TAB>少しくらい　お客さんが　そんをしても
<TAB>いいと思ってるかい？

entries.english: Douglas: "Would you let customers lose out a little if it meant more profit for your shop?"
entries.reason: Correct yes/no polarity: JP asks whether this is acceptable. Do you mind if reverses affirmative meaning. 322 approves the permissive answer; 323 rebukes softness.

entries.english: ???: "Torneko! You truly are the saviour of our kingdom!"

entries.english: ???: "All I thought about was getting out of difficult work. What a fool I've been."
entries.reason: Natural expression for trying to avoid difficult work.

entries.before: ???: "Torneko! You truly are the savior of our kingdom."
entries.english: ???: "Torneko! You truly are the saviour of our kingdom."
entries.reason: Consistent repeated wording and British spelling.

<TAB>ボクに　借りがあるんだからな。
<TAB>忘れるなよ。
entries.before: Prince: "Your father owes me a favor. Don't forget it."
entries.english: Prince: "Your father owes me a favour. Don't forget it."
entries.reason: Consistent British spelling; repeated armour examination matches the shared-story revision.

entries.japanese:
王子「そういえば　まだ　トルネコから
<TAB>貸しを　返してもらってなかったね。
entries.before: Prince: "Come to think of it, Torneko still owes me a favor."
entries.english: Prince: "Come to think of it, Torneko still owes me a favour."
entries.reason: Consistent British spelling; repeated armour examination matches the shared-story revision.

entries.japanese:
＊「あなたがたこそ
<TAB>わが国の救世主です！
<TAB>本当に　ありがとうございました！
entries.before: ???: "You are the saviors of our kingdom! Thank you so very much!"
entries.english: ???: "You are the saviours of our kingdom! Thank you so very much!"

  神経痛に　ひびくんだからさ。

entries.english: *Fortune-teller: Don't make an old woman overdo it! Zooming makes my aches flare up.
